pr_title: [Subtitles][Plugins] Do not browse plugin directory when browsing for…
pr_body:
… subtitles

## Description
If we use "browse for subtitles" when a `plugin://` item is being played, the root folder of the addon is displayed in the dialog. There's no way to move back or select an actual subtitle from the video shares. This PR avoids setting the path for plugin items, displaying all the available shares instead, restoring the actual functionality.

## Motivation and Context
Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/19276

## How Has This Been Tested?
Runtime tested

issue_context.title: In a Plugin: Unable to load subtitles outside virtual filesystem of plugin
issue_context.body:
Please see the referenced issue in the Kodi Netflix Addon: https://github.com/CastagnaIT/plugin.video.netflix/issues/1085#issuecomment-783979000 

### Bug
As a User, I'm unable to load custom subtitles for movies/series/media I watch inside a plugin, as the file browser for subtitles only has access to the virtual file system of the plugin. 

### Expected Behavior
As a User, when trying to load a custom subtitle, I want to be able to browse any of my media sources (e.g. filesystem on my raspberry pi, network share, etc.) for a subtitle file (e.g. a .srt file), load it and use it like with any media I would use from traditional media sources (smb, http, etc.). 

### Actual behavior
I'm limited to load files from the virtual filesystem of the plugin. For Plugins like e.g. Netflix or Amazon Prime Video, this filesystem is basically the list of movies available on that service. Obviously I'm unable to upload my custom .srt subtitle file to this service so that it would appear in that virtual filesystem, and thus, I'm unable to use .srt files for languages not natively supported by that Plugin/Service. 

According to @CastagnaIT , this is a bug/limitation in Kodi and not the Netflix Plugin. 

### Steps to reproduce
1. Store any subtitle .srt file on a media source which is configured in kodi, e.g. a network share
2. Start the Netflix Plugin, browse to a movie, start playing it
3. stop the movie, go to the subtitles menu, try loading a custom subtitle
4. current behavior: I'm unable to navigate to the network share where my subtitle file is located, thus unable to load it.
4. expected behavior: I'm able to browse past the limitations of the virtual filesystem of the plugin and thus be able to navigate to the network share where I have placed my .srt file.

## Possible Fix
@CastagnaIT mentioned, I would be able to work around this issue by moving the movie in netflix to my library. However, I was unable to do so, as I don't have "Libraries" configured but always directly use media sources (network shares). 


### Debuglog
The debuglog can be found here:
I currently don't have this at hand. If required, I can generate one - please let me know. 

### Your Environment
Used Operating system:
Kodi 18.9 on Raspberry PI 4 4GB via LibreELEC 9.2.6
